title: A unit peer correction raises bounded HARPS reduction-difference error by 51 percent in 387 nights
abstract: We test whether other stars observed on the same night predict the raw DRS minus SERVAL velocity difference in 19 existing HARPS-RVBank version 02 files. Time-block fits remove a separate linear trend and smooth Earth-velocity response for each star and instrument era. Residuals are bounded at 10 m/s. The test has 1365 star-night measurements on 387 nights from 18 stars. A unit correction from at least two other stars raises squared error from 13.286 to 20.128 (m/s)^2, a gain of -51.5 percent. A 30-day block resample range is -66.1 to -37.9 percent. Bounds of 5 and 20 m/s, a simpler trend and star deletion retain negative gain. A later test learns the correction strength from separate blocks. It gives 1.0 percent gain with a range from -1.3 to +3.1 percent. Thus this test establishes no useful peer correction for the selected reduction differences. It does not test the published quiet-star zero-point solution or exclude weak shared errors. Both reductions share spectra; no independent instrument or planet confirmation is supplied. The package has original code, aggregate results, a figure, exact source hashes and separate-scratch retrieval steps. External observation records stay outside the publication.
